messages:
mara: Heads-up — saw a steady memory growth on a dedicated node serving mixed workloads (short chat + occasional ~8k longcontexts). Heap looks fine but KV cache resident size creeps. :eyes:
hao: Can you paste the perf traces / jemalloc stats? sound like fragmentation but curious about allocation patterns.
sam: pinged infra for the node id, we can repro on staging.
mara: Node: rwin-stg-12, timeline attached below — here's the quick dump of slab buckets (snip):
```
slab: total=24G used=19.1G free_holes=13k avg_gap=384B top_buckets: 512B:3.2G, 2k:6.8G, 16k:5.6G, 64k:2.4G
free_blocks_by_size: 512: 120k, 2k: 40k, 16k: 3k, 64k: 600
```
mara: Notice the huge count of small free blocks (512B/2k) but large used in 16k/64k — looks like small-fragment holes everywhere.
jen: Do we still use fixed slab sizes (power-of-two) for KV pages? thought we added medium pool.
kevin: Allocator is power-of-two buckets with a small object slab for <4k, medium 4k-32k, large >32k. But long contexts cause many variable-sized KV pages that get split.
hao: Repro script I ran: ~30% longcontext requests (6k-8k tokens), rest 128 tokens. After ~12h steady QPS, free_small_blocks skyrockets.

sam: Logs from perf:
```
2026-01-18T03:12:41Z kvcache: alloc_small_requests=1.2M alloc_large_requests=80k
2026-01-18T03:12:41Z kvcache: avg_alloc_size=5.6k median=2.1k
2026-01-18T03:12:41Z kvcache: compaction_runs=2 last_run=+48h
```

mara: Important: compaction currently only runs at high free_count thresholds and is expensive (pauses). So it rarely fires on staging.
hao: Hypothesis: mixed workload leads to interleaved allocation/free patterns that leave small holes that never coalesce because adjacent freelist metadata remains in different slab classes. Buddy/coalesce not effective because of internal fragmentation.
jen: Can we tune block sizes? e.g., reduce small bucket granularity to avoid many 512B holes? That might increase internal fragmentation for other workloads.
kevin: Idea: adaptive slab hysteresis — dynamically promote medium slab size when we detect >X% longcontext requests for T minutes, which reduces splitting of large KV pages into many small fragments. When longcontext load subsides, demote.
hao: Also propose an "idle compactor" that scans candidate slabs during low CPU and performs local compaction with bounded CPU/latency. Conditions: cpu_idle > 40% && fragmentation_ratio > 0.25 && compaction_budget_ms < 200.
sam: Love the two-pronged approach. Adaptive slab sizing reduces new fragmentation; idle compactor consolidates existing holes.
jen: Need safety: compaction must be interruptible and should not block requests. Do it per-slab in small steps.
kevin: Prototype config I tested locally (rough):
```
kvcache.adaptive_slab.enabled = true
kvcache.adaptive_slab.longcontext_threshold = 0.25
kvcache.adaptive_slab.promotion_window_s = 300
kvcache.idle_compactor.enabled = true
kvcache.idle_compactor.cpu_idle_pct = 40
kvcache.idle_compactor.max_ms_per_cycle = 150
kvcache.idle_compactor.min_fragmentation = 0.20
```
kevin: With that on staging, the resident size stabilized after ~6h in my run. Avg fragmentation ratio dropped from 0.31 -> 0.18.

mara: Can you share numbers? especially p95 latency impact during compaction?
kevin: p50/p95 generator latencies: baseline p95=76ms, with adaptive-slab only p95=80ms (+4ms), with idle compactor running p95 up to 95ms during compaction windows but compactor runs in tiny slices and recovers. Overall tail improved after compaction ended.
hao: We should pick safe defaults: short promotion_window (e.g. 2m) to avoid oscillation; add hysteresis so we only demote after longcontext_fraction < threshold for 10m. Also add a rate limit on slab promotions.
sam: How invasive is this change? allocator layer only? can we A/B via config flags?
kevin: Yes allocator-only change and idle compactor is an optional background thread. Can be gated via runtime flag (rollout via console per-dedicated cluster).
jen: Testing plan:
- run 48h mixed workload canary on 3 nodes with synthetic mix (30% longcontext)
- metric targets: fragmentation_ratio < 0.22, resident_growth < 200MB/day, p95 request latency < +10ms
- failover: if p95 > +20ms for 10m, auto-disable

mara: Also let's add a diagnostic metric: slab_promotions, compaction_slices, compaction_cpu_ms so we can tune later.
hao: One more gotcha: model KV shapes differ (decoder-only vs. encoder-decoder). Need to validate on both. I saw different bucket distributions when running t5-like model.
kevin: Agreed — doing cross-model stress next.
sam: I'll draft a short RFC with config knobs and canary plan. Mara, can you paste the staging perf trace you captured so I can include graphs?
mara: Pasting small CSV excerpt and an ascii sparkline in the RFC. Also attaching the quick repro script: (run under perf harness)
```
# repro.sh
for i in $(seq 1 2000); do
  if [ $((RANDOM%10)) -lt 3 ]; then
    ./client --tokens 7000
  else
    ./client --tokens 128
  fi
  sleep 0.02
done
```

jen: thanks. small note — make sure compactor honors memory pressure signals; we don't want it to run when cgroup mem.available is low.
kevin: added to TODO.
perf-bot: Experiment started: canary kvcache.adaptive_slab=on on cluster=stg-canary-5 at 2026-02-02T14:10Z — will report metrics every 10m.
mara: OK, next steps: RFC (sam), small prototype PR (kevin) with off-by-default config, perf run (perf-bot), and cross-model tests (hao). I'll watch staging. Thanks everyone. :thumbsup:
